name: Mahindra EPC Irrigation Ltd
title: Mahindra EPC Irrigation Ltd - 523754 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.8% to INR315.8 crores and PBT to INR16.99 crores, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores on a March raw-material spike.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR315.8 crores (up 14.8% from INR275.1 crores) and PBT of INR16.99 crores versus INR10.7 crores in FY25, despite a INR2.1 crore past-service personnel cost. Q4 revenue grew about 11%, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores from INR9.4 crores as PE pipe prices jumped roughly 58-59% in February 2026 and stayed high in March. Receivables built up sharply in a few key subsidy states, and operating free cash flow has been negative over multi-year periods, which an analyst pressed on. Management pointed to non-subsidy share rising to 35% in FY26 (from 3% in FY20 per the call) and to a projects pipeline of about INR54-55 crores for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR10.7 crores in FY25; after INR2.1 crore past-service personnel cost
vs INR9.4 crores in Q4 FY25
Higher than previous year; 80-90% from subsidy business
from 2% in FY20 (management also cited 3% in FY20 in the call)

financial_highlights.value: Negative over 3, 4 and 5 years as stated by analyst
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited -INR18 crores (3 yrs), zero (4 yrs), -INR22 crores (5 yrs); not disputed by management

segments.name: Subsidy business
segments.commentary: About 65% of FY26 revenue; receivables pile-up is concentrated here, with states in the south and west (two south, one west) cited for delayed payments. Management says 80-90% of receivables come from this segment.

segments.name: Non-subsidy business
segments.commentary: About 35% of FY26 revenue, an all-time high, spanning projects, ISI-grade farmer sales, institutional sales, thin-wall pipes and mulch sheets. Management expects this share to keep rising, with no timeline given.

segments.name: Irrigation projects (government tenders)
segments.commentary: About a quarter of total business (about INR75 crores per analyst's math, confirmed as a quarter). Opening FY27 order visibility is INR54 crores, with a possible further INR20 crores in coming weeks. Projects drive higher variable/other expenses but lower raw-material cost.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh / North India
segments.commentary: Early-stage expansion; UP revenue grew about 28% in FY26 after two exploratory years.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance on margins or EBITDA; management said it does not give outlooks.
Raw material prices expected to stay range-bound once geopolitical tensions ease, but not back to FY20 levels; caution flagged for Q1 FY27.
Industry industry-association representation to government for a subsidy/price increase is pending; timing not given.
Management expects a pickup in the non-subsidy share and in receivable collections from key states, but gave no timeline (said collections expected 'imminently').
Management said it is preparing a step-up in project size (beyond current INR5-20 crore projects), but not a significant jump.
capex_capacity: Management said capex plans exist every year, focused on productivity and on current product lines; no amount was disclosed.
Satellite manufacturing units complement the main Nashik plant; this has improved asset utilisation and freight/processing cost control.
Recent equipment investment has cut electricity costs, cited as an example of quick-payback capex.
New product-line investment will follow once new non-subsidy lines are established.
demand_pricing: Industry FY26 growth estimated at 6-7% versus company's 14.8%; FY25 industry demand about 1 million hectares versus 1.1 million in FY24.
Government target of 2 million hectares a year (10 million over five years) versus about 1 million in FY25.
Above-normal monsoon (107.9% of LPA) hurt H1 FY26 demand; H2 was stronger. Management flagged possible El Nino in FY27 and a below-normal monsoon risk, with impact expected more in H2.
Raw material (PE pipe) prices rose about 58-59% in February 2026 with supply constraints; company is seeking price increases mainly in non-subsidy, with subsidy prices set by government.
GST cut from 12% to 5% seen as a medium-term demand positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material price increase is expected for FY27, how much can be passed on, and what is the EBITDA margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called raw material volatility an FY27 risk, with mitigation via product mix, geography mix and timing of procurement. It declined to give a margin target and said it would selectively raise prices in non-subsidy markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a higher share of projects revenue in Q4, which carries higher variable expenses but lower raw-material cost, plus some cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow has been negative over several years; when will the non-subsidy mix invert, and how much of INR217 crore receivables is non-subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-90% of receivables are from subsidy business. It expects cash flows to improve as two southern states and one western state resume payments, and cited thin-wall and mulch sheet products with better cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for capex in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is planned annually, mainly for productivity and current product lines, with capacity expansion secondary; management expects quick payback on each spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the new labour code and contractual alignment of employee benefits; not headcount additions or variable pay.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of below-normal monsoon on demand, and timing of government price action?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects any monsoon impact to show mainly in H2 FY27 and is monitoring it. Price relief via the government is a daily discussion with no date; difficult to call.

qa_highlights.question: Project size and FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Plans to step up project size, not drastically. Opening order visibility is INR54 crores (earlier cited 55), with a possible INR20 crore upside.

risks_watch: Raw material (PE pipe) price volatility and geopolitical risk; margin pressure in Q1 FY27 if prices stay high and government price revision is delayed.
Receivables in key subsidy states (INR217 crores closing); collections and NABARD-type interventions are not yet confirmed.
Negative operating free cash flow across multi-year periods; reliance on borrowings for working capital.
Weak or below-normal monsoon in FY27 could hit H2 demand.
Government fund release delays and state-level execution risk; subsidy share still about 65%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term industry and business-mix strategy, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, pricing and cash-flow timing. Management avoided numerical outlooks and gave no dates for price relief or receivable collections.
key_quotes: Despite all these challenges, your company registered its highest ever revenue in FY26.
We don't tend to give outlooks.
So we do believe that as collections normalize, the cash flows will improve.
There is definitely visibility for the INR55 crores, it's actually INR54 crores.

growth.why: Management gives no numeric outlook; only visible support is an opening FY27 project order book of INR54 crores (possibly INR20 crores more), with pending subsidy price hike and no timeline on non-subsidy share gains or collections; no new capacity is quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores from INR9.4 crores as PE pipe prices jumped about 58-59% in February 2026; management flagged Q1 FY27 caution and gave no margin target, with price relief from government undated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Opening FY27 project order book of INR54 crores (possibly INR20 crores more) and non-subsidy share at 35% support volumes, but a possible El Nino and below-normal monsoon could hit H2 demand and management gave no volume outlook.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says capex is planned every year for productivity and current lines with no amount disclosed; UP revenue grew about 28% but no utilisation figure was given to justify a new-capacity announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no numeric outlook and cited raw-material volatility and receivable delays as FY27 risks.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 PBT fell about 32% YoY to INR6.4 crores on the PE price spike, and management flagged Q1 FY27 caution with possible monsoon impact in H2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said new product-line investment will follow once new non-subsidy lines are established, with thin-wall pipes and mulch sheets cited as better cash-flow products; no launch date given.

rows.label: Receivables recovery in southern and western subsidy states
rows.why: Closing receivables are INR217 crores, 80-90% from subsidy business, and management expects collections 'imminently' but gave no date; operating FCF negative over 3-5 years.

rows.label: Government subsidy price revision and non-subsidy price increases
rows.why: Industry representation for a subsidy price hike is pending with no timing, and management plans selective non-subsidy price increases against PE costs up about 58-59%.

rows.label: Opening FY27 project order book
rows.why: Opening visibility is INR54 crores with a possible INR20 crores more in coming weeks, against FY26 revenue of INR315.8 crores, about 17% of the year's revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term industry growth and the non-subsidy mix shift to 35%, but cautious and non-committal on Q1 FY27 margins, price relief and receivable collection timing; analysts pressed on negative multi-year operating cash flow and the INR217 crore receivables build-up.
